passage:
I share a room with my cousin Jasleen during her board exams, so I saw it all. First it was one can of energy drink at night. Then two, then one at breakfast too. By the second week her hands shook when she held her pen, and she'd jump if I dropped a book. At two in the morning she'd still be awake, staring at the ceiling, whispering formulas. In the chemistry exam, she told me later, her mind went fuzzy and her heart raced. I don't know exactly what was happening inside her. But after that, our Bua sat with her, gently took the cans away and made a plan with her: sleep by eleven, proper meals, a walk between chapters, and the doctor if her heart kept racing. By the next paper, Jasleen was calmer.
Deepika

qa.q: At what time would Jasleen still be awake?
qa.a: At two in the morning.

qa.q: What might Jasleen's shaking hands and jumpiness suggest?
qa.a: They suggest Jasleen was anxious and jittery from the energy drinks and lack of sleep, though Deepika could not be sure.

qa.q: What plan did Bua make, and why is it better fuel?
qa.a: Sleep by eleven, proper meals and a walk between chapters, which steady body and mind instead of leading to a jittery crash.

qa.q: How was Deepika affected by sharing the room?
qa.a: Deepika saw the shaking, jumpiness and sleepless nights up close and seemed worried.

grounding: A teenager relying on energy drinks for exams becomes shaky, anxious and sleepless, and sleep, food and breaks prove better fuel.

passage:
Monday. Mohit bought two energy drinks on the way home and studied till three. His heart was drumming, and when he finally lay down, his legs wouldn't keep still.
Wednesday. After two nights like that, he walked into the physics test shaking. He read the first question three times. His classmate Farida noticed his hand trembling and asked if he was okay. "Too much caffeine, no sleep," he muttered. He left half the paper blank.
The following Monday. No cans. He was asleep by eleven, ate his mother's poha, and took a short walk between chapters. Before the maths test Farida asked again. "Tired," Mohit said, "but not buzzing." He finished the paper.

qa.q: How many energy drinks did Mohit buy on Monday?
qa.a: Mohit bought two energy drinks.

qa.q: How did Mohit feel walking into the physics test?
qa.a: Mohit felt shaky and anxious, rereading the first question and unable to focus.

qa.q: What changed before the maths test, and why did it help?
qa.a: No cans, sleep by eleven, breakfast and short walks between chapters, so Mohit was tired but not buzzing.

qa.q: What did Farida notice?
qa.a: Farida noticed Mohit's hand trembling and cared enough to ask if he was okay.

grounding: A teenager using energy drinks to study late becomes shaky and sleepless, and sleep, food and breaks prove better fuel.

passage: It was the week of her final school exams in Buenos Aires, and Valentina had been living on energy drinks. One after dinner, another at midnight, another at two. She studied till four, but by the next morning her hands were shaking, her heart was racing, and her thoughts skittered like marbles. She couldn't remember a thing she'd read. That night she couldn't sleep at all, even though she was exhausted, and the next day was worse. Her older sister Rania found the empty cans stacked behind her desk. 'Vale, these are making you jittery, not smart.' Rania took the cans away, made her a proper dinner, and set an alarm for bedtime at eleven. 'Short breaks, real food, real sleep.' Two days later, Valentina walked into her history exam tired but steady.

qa.q: Where did Rania find the empty cans?
qa.a: Stacked behind Valentina's desk.

qa.q: How did Valentina feel the morning after studying till four?
qa.a: She felt shaky and anxious, with a racing heart and scattered thoughts.

qa.q: What did Rania change for Valentina?
qa.a: She took the cans away, made a proper dinner and set a bedtime, with short breaks, real food and real sleep.

qa.q: How might Rania have felt finding the cans?
qa.a: She was probably worried and a little alarmed at how much Valentina was relying on them.

grounding: Shows a teenager relying on energy drinks to study late who becomes shaky, anxious and sleepless, and how sleep, food and breaks work better.

passage: In the coaching institute hostel in Kota, the vending machine by the stairs sold energy drinks, and by December Vinita was buying them every night. She was preparing for the medical entrance and sleeping four hours. During Tuesday's mock test, her hands trembled so badly her OMR marks went outside the circles. Her heart hammered. She felt like crying for no reason. Her friend Farhan found her afterwards on the stairs. 'You're shaking. Are those drinks helping?' Vinita laughed shakily. 'I can't sleep without being tired and I can't study without them.' Farhan took her to the hostel nurse, who checked her pulse and told her kindly that sleep and regular meals would do more than any can. Vinita started studying in the morning instead, with breaks, and slept by midnight.

qa.q: What did the vending machine by the stairs sell?
qa.a: Energy drinks.

qa.q: How was Vinita feeling during Tuesday's mock test?
qa.a: She felt shaky and anxious, with a hammering heart and a strange urge to cry.

qa.q: What did the nurse suggest instead of the drinks?
qa.a: That sleep and regular meals would help more than any can.

qa.q: How might Farhan have felt seeing Vinita shake on the stairs?
qa.a: He was probably worried about her and wanted to help her get proper support.

grounding: Shows a teenager relying on energy drinks to stay up for exams who becomes shaky, anxious and unable to sleep, and learns sleep, food and breaks are better fuel.

passage:
Dear Aadhya,
Maasi says you've started drinking energy drinks to study for your boards. I'm writing because I did exactly that last year, and I wish someone had told me the truth.
The first night, it felt great. I studied till three. But the next day my hands were shaking and my heart kept racing, and I felt anxious about nothing. That night I couldn't sleep at all, so I needed another can to wake up. By the end of the week I was jittery, snappy and remembering less than before.
What actually worked: going to bed by eleven, eating proper meals, and taking a ten-minute walk every hour. Boring, I know. But my marks went up when I stopped.
Call me if you want to talk about the exams.
Kiran

qa.q: What time did Kiran go to bed once things improved?
qa.a: By eleven.

qa.q: How did Kiran feel by the end of the week on energy drinks?
qa.a: Kiran felt jittery, snappy and anxious, and remembered less than before.

qa.q: What does Kiran suggest instead of energy drinks?
qa.a: Going to bed by eleven, eating proper meals and taking a ten-minute walk every hour.

qa.q: How might Aadhya feel reading this letter?
qa.a: Aadhya may feel a bit caught out but also cared for, and more likely to listen to someone who has been there.

grounding: Shows a teenager who relied on energy drinks for exams, became shaky, anxious and sleepless, and learned that sleep, food and breaks are better fuel.

passage: Uma, you asked why I look like a zombie, so here's the story. Board prep week, right? I'm Ritu, the girl who thinks she can beat biology in five nights. So I bought those tall energy drinks from the corner shop, a couple every night, and studied till three. First night I felt like a superhero. Second night my hands were shaking over the diagram of the heart, my own heart was thumping, and I couldn't sleep even when I lay down at four. Next morning I blanked on a question I knew. Then I panicked, drank another can, and the whole thing repeated. On Friday Papa found three cans in my bin and sat with me instead of shouting. Now it's lights off by eleven-thirty, a proper dinner, and a short walk between chapters. My hands are steady again, Uma.

qa.q: What did Papa find in Ritu's bin?
qa.a: He found three cans.

qa.q: What was Ritu feeling on the second night, and what are the signs?
qa.a: She felt jittery and anxious; her hands shook, her heart thumped and she couldn't sleep.

qa.q: What changed after Friday, and why is it better fuel for exams?
qa.a: Ritu now sleeps by eleven-thirty, eats a proper dinner and takes short walking breaks, which keep her steady instead of shaky.

qa.q: How might Papa have felt finding the cans?
qa.a: Papa was probably worried, but chose to sit with Ritu calmly, which made it easier for her to change.
